newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds outshone the bloc again.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds outshone the bloc again.

text.p: Australian bonds outperformed the rest of the dollar bloc for the second successive session, continuning to claw back last week's spread widening.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread broke back below 100 basis points amid offshore buying of the local market and speculation of a further easing in monetary policy. Such talk coincided with today's monthly Reserve Bank board meeting.
Meanwhile, Treasury yields were little changed in Tokyo trading after ending stable in New York with a brief upward spike following a stronger than expected November NAPM index proving shortlived.
Canadian bonds underperformed on supply concerns after the Canadian government said it would auction C$3.0 billion of two-year bonds on Friday.
Against New Zealand the spread narrowing was slightly more tame as the market there rallied on a strong N.Z. dollar and bullishness ahead of the RBNZ's Monetary Policy Statement on December 17.
